prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2017 – summary (under 500 words)

Pitch and purpose
- Make the Liberal Democrats a strong, independent opposition (no coalition with Conservatives or Labour), holding the government to account and championing an open, tolerant, united Britain.

Europe and Brexit
- Oppose a hard Brexit; keep the UK as close to the EU as possible.
- Second referendum on the final deal, with the option to remain.
- Seek single market and customs union participation; protect freedom of movement; guarantee rights for EU citizens in the UK and UK citizens in the EU.
- Safeguard Erasmus+, research funding, environmental and social protections, policing cooperation (Europol/EAW), and consumer benefits (EHIC, roaming).

NHS and social care
- Immediate 1p Income Tax rise (c. £6bn) ringfenced for NHS and social care; plan a dedicated health and care tax.
- Cross-party convention and an independent budget office for health and care.
- Integrate NHS and social care; cap care costs; support carers.
- End public sector pay cap, reinstate nurse bursaries, protect EU staff.
- Parity for mental health: enforce waiting standards, expand talking therapies, crisis care, perinatal and youth services.

Education and young people
- Reverse school/college cuts; protect per-pupil funding; fair national formula; nearly £7bn extra incl. Pupil Premium; triple Early Years Pupil Premium.
- Oppose new grammar schools; restore local authority role in places and standards.
- End 1% cap on teacher pay; guaranteed CPD; cut workload.
- Slim national curriculum incl. PSHE/SRE (with LGBT+ content), arts protected; better careers/vocational routes.
- Expand mental health support in schools; free school meals for all primaries; breakfast clubs.
- Universities: restore maintenance grants; protect research and international staff; review finance; maintain openness post‑Brexit.

Economy, work and business
- Eliminate day-to-day deficit by 2020; borrow to invest £100bn in housing (300k homes/yr), schools/hospitals, transport (HS2/CR2), and hyperfast fibre.
- Create a Housing & Infrastructure Bank; support SMEs/start‑ups.
- Fairer taxes: reverse recent cuts (e.g., Corporation Tax to 17%, CGT cuts, Marriage Allowance, higher IHT threshold), tackle avoidance, review business rates and consider land value tax.
- Promote living wage, transparency on pay ratios; modernise gig‑economy rights; curb zero‑hours abuse; scrap tribunal fees.

Environment and energy
- Five green laws: transport, zero‑carbon, nature, buildings, zero‑waste.
- Air Quality Plan; diesel car/small van sales ban by 2025; expand ULEZs; boost EV infrastructure.
- Target 60% electricity from renewables by 2030; net‑zero by 2050; back storage, smart grids, CCS; oppose fracking; conditional support for new nuclear; keep Euratom.
- Insulate 4m homes by 2022; restore zero‑carbon homes; expand community energy.
- Nature Act, flood fund, stronger farming/animal welfare; 70% recycling, coffee‑cup levy.

Homes, transport, communities
- Build 300k homes/yr incl. 500k affordable; 10 garden cities; lift council borrowing cap; strengthen affordable obligations.
- Renting: ban letting fees, cap deposits, longer tenancies, Help to Rent, Rent to Own; tackle rough sleeping with Housing First.
- Transport: rail reform and electrification; HS2/HS3/Crossrail 2/East‑West Rail; Young Person’s Bus Card (16–21); devolve bus powers; boost cycling/walking.

Rights, justice, immigration
- Defend HRA/ECHR; digital bill of rights; stronger FOI and press standards.
- £300m for community policing; body‑cams; replace PCCs; victims’ rights; presumption against short prison terms; Women’s Justice Board.
- Drug reform: end imprisonment for possession; legal, regulated cannabis.
- Positive, managed immigration: annual skills debate; remove students from targets; STEM post‑study visas; Migration Impact Fund; ESOL.
- Refugees: resettle 50,000 Syrians; reopen Dubs (3,000 children); 28‑day detention limit; faster asylum; protect LGBT+ asylum seekers.

International and defence
- Support UN/NATO; spend 0.7% on aid; tighter arms export controls; suspend sales to Saudi Arabia.
- Defence at 2% of GDP; cyber investment; minimum nuclear deterrent (3‑boat Dreadnought, non‑continuous patrols).

Political reform and devolution
- Votes at 16; STV for Westminster and local elections; reform Lords; cap donations at £10k; stronger lobbying rules; constitutional convention and written constitution.
- Devolution on demand in England; more powers for Wales; uphold NI settlement; oppose a second Scottish independence referendum.
